daily_load_assessment: Current CTL is 12.9 with an ATL of 6.6, yielding a positive TSB (+6.3). You are completely fresh and fully recovered following recent low volume. Immediate training stress is negligible, providing a clean slate to begin progressive overload today.
acute_status_assessment_3_weeks: Over the past 21 days, training volume has dropped significantly with very low acute load accumulation. Adaptation has stalled due to lack of consistency. Re-establishing regular daily training load is necessary to rebuild your momentum toward the CTL target.
sport_trend_assessment_6_months: The 6-month macro trend reflects intermittent training spikes followed by prolonged lulls. To reach your target CTL of 60 safely, you need a disciplined, steady ramp rate of +1 to +2 CTL per week, maintaining a strict 70/30 pyramidal distribution.
coach_verdict: Because acute fatigue is low and freshness is high, Priority 1 is a structured Zone 2 Aerobic Run to rebuild running load tolerance and aerobic base. Priority 2 is a Sweet Spot cycling session to build FTP endurance, and Priority 3 is a heavy strength session to support cycling torque and core stability.

priority_1.workout_details: 10 min Zone 1 warm-up; 40 min steady Zone 2 run targeting high leg turnover (175+ spm); 10 min cool-down walk.
priority_1.reason: Top priority to re-introduce impact load safely, build aerobic engine volume, and align with the 70% base training rule.

priority_2.workout_details: 15 min Zone 2 warm-up with 3x30s high-cadence spin-ups; 3x8 min @ 230W with 3 min Zone 1 recovery; 15 min Zone 2 cool-down.
priority_2.reason: Directly targets 20-minute power and FTP development with high time efficiency and manageable acute fatigue.

priority_3.workout_details: Barbell Back Squat: 4x6 @ 80kg; Romanian Deadlift: 3x8 @ 70kg; Overhead Press: 3x8 @ 40kg; Sandbag Carry: 4x30m (70kg); Hanging Leg Raises: 3x12.
priority_3.reason: Builds lower-body torque output for cycling, protects running leg stiffness, and satisfies upper-body aesthetic goals.
